title: Location Tracking via GPS Data in Transit
description: GPS position data transmitted through the data flow can be intercepted or logged, enabling tracking of the user's movements and location history over time. This creates a persistent record of the user's physical whereabouts that could be linked to their identity.

title: User Identification via Sensor Data Patterns
description: The combination of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps in transit can create a unique behavioral fingerprint that identifies the user, especially when correlated with other data sources or when the data is intercepted.

title: Voluntary Data Sharing Enables Identification
description: The user's act of wearing the device and sharing continuous sensor telemetry creates a data trail that can be used to identify the user, as the data patterns are inherently tied to the individual wearer.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage and Processing at Destination
description: The wearable device (P1) may store or process the captured sensor data in ways that exceed the user's consent or intended purpose, potentially leading to unauthorized access, profiling, or sharing with third parties.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Sensor data including GPS traces, device IDs, and timestamps transmitted between wearable device and companion app could be intercepted by third parties during transit, enabling identification of the user's location and activities.

title: Linkability of Data Across Sessions
description: Timestamps and device IDs in transmitted sensor batches could be used to link multiple data sessions to the same user, enabling tracking of movement patterns and behavior over time.

title: Identification Through Device Data Sharing
description: The wearable device shares device IDs and unique sensor data that could be used to identify the specific user, especially when combined with GPS traces that reveal location patterns.

title: Unauthorized Data Access at Destination
description: The companion mobile app receives and stores sensitive personal data including GPS traces and device identifiers, creating risk of unauthorized access or improper handling of user location and activity information.

title: Excessive Data Collection and Storage
description: The companion app may collect and store more data than necessary for its intended function, including detailed GPS traces and device identifiers that could be retained longer than needed, increasing privacy exposure.

title: Linkability of health data in transit
description: Calorie, meal, and weight data transmitted in this flow could be linked to the user through metadata or data patterns, potentially revealing identity or associations with other data sources.

title: Identification through health data sharing
description: Manual logging of weight, calorie, and meal data by the user could be used to identify them, especially if this data is combined with other information or metadata.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: The companion app may store or process the user's sensitive health data in a way that exposes it to unauthorized access, third parties, or unintended recipients.

title: Excessive data collection in health tracking
description: The app may collect more health data than necessary for the stated purpose of calorie and weight tracking, potentially including unnecessary personal information.

title: Unauthorized access to user's health data
description: If the user's device is compromised or authentication is weak, someone could potentially access or manipulate the health data being entered into the app.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Health log data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) transmitted from the mobile app to the health log store could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive personal health information.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Health Data
description: Once stored in the health log store, the sensitive health data could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems without proper access controls, leading to privacy violations.

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Transit
description: Health log data could be altered or tampered with during transmission between the app and data store, potentially leading to inaccurate health records or manipulation of exercise and dietary data.

title: Data Integrity Compromise at Rest
description: Stored health data in the health log store could be corrupted or modified by malicious actors with access to the storage system, compromising the accuracy and reliability of health records.

title: Identification via Health Data Patterns
description: Even if individual health log entries are anonymized, patterns in the data (e.g., exercise frequency, weight changes, dietary habits) could be used to identify or re-identify the user through correlation with other data sources.

title: Unauthorized User Access to Health Records
description: The health log store could be accessed by unauthorized users who impersonate legitimate users or exploit authentication weaknesses, gaining access to personal health information.

title: Lack of User Control Over Data Sharing
description: Users of the companion mobile app may have limited control over who can access their health log data once it is shared with the health log store, potentially leading to unwanted data exposure.

title: Identification through location data collection
description: The mobile app collects and stores precise GPS location traces with timestamps, which can be used to identify individuals based on their movement patterns and routines.

title: Linkability through location metadata
description: Location data with timestamps in transit can be linked to other data sources or used to correlate activities, potentially revealing sensitive information about the user's whereabouts and associations.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location history
description: The location history store may be accessible to unauthorized parties or may leak location data through improper access controls, exposing users' movement patterns.

title: Data misuse for secondary purposes
description: Stored location history may be used for purposes beyond the original consent, such as profiling, advertising, or sharing with third parties without user knowledge.

title: Individual identification through health log pattern analysis
description: The analytics service processes health logs across sessions, potentially enabling identification of individuals through behavioral patterns in calorie, weight, and exercise data

title: Linkability of health data through session patterns
description: Health logs across multiple sessions could be correlated to link data to specific individuals, even without explicit identifiers

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health data
description: The analytics service may lack proper access controls, potentially allowing unauthorized access to or disclosure of sensitive health information

title: User unawareness of health data analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed for health-condition analysis, violating transparency expectations

title: Location Data Interception in Transit
description: Location history data transmitted from datastore to analytics service could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling identification of individuals through their movement patterns.

title: Linkability of Location Patterns
description: Location data in transit could be linked with other data sources to create comprehensive profiles of individuals' daily routines and movement patterns.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure at Destination
description: Health Analytics Service may store, share, or retain location history data beyond intended purposes, potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns to unauthorized parties.

title: Unawareness of Location Analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed to derive daily routine and movement patterns, violating informed consent principles.

title: Identification Through Location Sharing
description: The act of sharing location history data from the datastore could directly identify individuals based on their unique movement patterns and location data.

title: Inferred Health Insights May Reveal Identifiable Information
description: The Health Analytics Service shares inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that could potentially identify individuals when combined with other data sources or metadata.

title: Health Data in Transit May Be Linked Across Systems
description: Data in transit between the Health Analytics Service and Companion Mobile App could be intercepted and linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive health profile of the user.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Insights at Destination
description: The Companion Mobile App may store or process the received health insights in ways that lead to unauthorized disclosure, such as through insecure storage, sharing with third parties, or improper access controls.

title: Usurpation of Health Data by Malicious Actors
description: The Companion Mobile App could be compromised, allowing malicious actors to access, manipulate, or misuse the health-condition risk indicators and trend flags.

title: Unauthorized Information Disclosure of Health Indicators
description: The mobile app displays sensitive health risk indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through screen capture, network interception, or improper access controls.

title: Health Condition Identification Risk
description: The displayed health risk indicators could be used to identify the user's medical condition to third parties, potentially leading to discrimination or stigma.

title: Psychological Harm from Health Risk Display
description: Displaying inferred health risk signals to the user may cause psychological distress, anxiety, or unintended behavioral consequences without proper medical context or professional guidance.

title: Inaccurate Health Indicator Presentation
description: The app may present inaccurate or misleading health risk indicators based on algorithmic inference, leading to poor health decisions or unnecessary medical concern.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Health data, models, and location datasets transmitted to the cloud provider could be intercepted by malicious actors during transit, enabling identification of individuals through the sensitive health and location information.

title: Metadata Exposure in Transit
description: Metadata accompanying the data flow (e.g., sender/receiver identifiers, timestamps, data sizes) could be used to link or identify individuals and infer sensitive information about the health analytics service and its users.

title: Unauthorized Access by Cloud Provider Personnel
description: Cloud hosting provider employees or contractors with access to the hosted data could improperly access, view, or copy the full health and location datasets, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal information.

title: Data Misuse by Third-Party Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may use the hosted health analytics data, models, or location datasets for purposes beyond the agreed hosting arrangement, such as selling data to third parties or using it for their own analytics.

title: Re-identification from Hosted Data
description: The full health and location dataset hosted at the cloud provider could be re-identified through cross-referencing with other publicly available data, compromising the anonymity of individuals whose data is stored.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) regarding the storage and processing of health data, leading to legal and compliance risks.
